newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Winnie Mandela faces hefty travel bill.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Winnie Mandela faces hefty travel bill.

text.p: South African legislator Winnie Mandela might soon have to repay the cost of an unauthorised foreign trip that caused her husband, President Nelson Mandela, to fire her from his government last year, officials said.
Ken Andrew, chairman of parliament's watchdog public accounts committee, on Wednesday said Mrs Mandela's colleagues had refused to sanction a 112,000 rand ($23,800) trip to Ghana in March last year.
He said the committee would invite Mrs Mandela, whose marriage to the president ended in a messy public divorce this year, to offer an explanation for the trip.
If she failed to offer a satisfactory explanation, the government would try to recover the money from her.
"On the basis of the evidence before us at present, we are not in a position to authorise the expenditure," Andrew said.
Mrs Mandela, at the time deputy minister of arts, culture, science and technology, visited a film festival in Ghana after the president had ordered her to cancel the trip.
She was dismissed on her return, but won a court order forcing him briefly to reinstate her and then to go through the dismissal procedures more carefully.
After her dismissal as a deputy minister Mrs Mandela remained a member of the national assembly.
